findings.finding: The street sits below the company's own revenue guide: FY26 revenue consensus is $13.06bn against Vertex's August-raised $13.1-13.2bn range (H1 actual $6.32bn, so the guide needs H2 $6.78-6.88bn versus ~$6.74bn implied by consensus), and Vertex beat Q2 revenue $3.33bn vs a $3.23bn Zacks consensus; a Q3 print at guide pace (~$3.42-3.45bn) clears the $3.39-3.40bn bar by ~1%, and a reaffirmed or nudged-up revenue guide is the likely shape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-03): revenue beat ~$100m and FY guide raised, but EPS $4.73 missed $4.79; stock closed +1.7% against a +/-5.8% implied move (EarningsWatcher). Q1 2026 (2026-05-04): -1.3%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-12): +5.7%. Revenue beats on this name are bought modestly, not strongly.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed the guide, FY consensus would sit at or above $13.1bn rather than $13.06bn; the gap is the street's own visible scepticism. The whisper number ($5.10 vs $4.92) suggests buy-side expects a beat, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 release (company primary document) for the H1 revenue and the guide: https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results ; Q1 2026 revenue $2.99bn: https://news.vrtx.com/node/34876 ; Q2 revenue beat vs Zacks: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/vrtxs-new-drugs-performance-mixed-q3-can-their-sales-improve (aggregated snippet).

findings.finding: Margin and opex pressure into H2: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was ~85.6% and management flagged larger mix and manufacturing headwinds in the back half, with non-GAAP opex tracking to the high end of $5.65-5.75bn; Q2 EPS already missed ($4.73 vs $4.79) on a revenue beat, so an EPS shortfall on a revenue beat can repeat -- but the EPS bar itself is disputed ($4.80 vs $4.92).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS miss with revenue beat and raise closed +1.7%, so an EPS miss alone was not punished last time.
findings.why_not_priced: The headwind is company-flagged, so partly in the bar; the disagreement between $4.80 and $4.92 consensus means some models carry the margin step-down and some do not. If fully priced the whisper would not sit above consensus.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 release (opex guide, gross margin derivable from product revenue and cost of sales): https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results . Same Finviz preview as finding 1 (shared document).

findings.finding: First guidance consolidating Crinetics (closed 2026-09-01, $8.8bn net of cash, partly funded with a $4.5bn term loan): Crinetics ran a $120.9m Q2 net loss on $24.0m of Palsonify net product revenue, so four months of consolidation adds roughly $40-60m of revenue and well over $100m of opex plus term-loan interest; Vertex has said the deal is not accretive to non-GAAP operating income until 2029 and promised the financial details on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deal announcement 2026-07-06: shares declined after hours (Las Vegas Sun/AP). No prior guide update on an acquisition of this size in the window history.
findings.why_not_priced: Direction is public but the magnitude is not: Crinetics withdrew its own guidance and held no call, so the street has no company number for 2026-27 opex or Palsonify trajectory; a larger-than-modelled opex step or a 2027 framework that pushes margin down would be new. The financing is for an approved, growing product plus a Phase 3 CAH asset, so it is a dilution question, not distress.
findings.independence: Vertex close release 2026-09-01 (financial details deferred to Q3 call), summarised via https://www.pharmexec.com/view/vertex-acquire-crinetics-10-billion and https://www.financierworldwide.com/fw-news/2026/7/9/vertex-to-acquire-crinetics-in-a-10bn-deal ; Q2 release states guidance excludes Crinetics: https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results

findings.finding: CF growth loses tailwinds in H2: CF grew 12% in Q2 with ex-US revenue up 14% helped by FX (FY guide includes ~150bp FX benefit), and the preview notes H2 CF growth faces less help from prior-year pricing and currency; Trikafta itself fell ($2,497m vs $2,551m) as patients switch to Alyftrek ($574m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: an Alyftrek line roughly at consensus with a Casgevy miss closed -1.0% (EarningsWatcher; Fierce Pharma coverage).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the FY consensus already sits below the guide (finding 1). This is the mechanism behind that scepticism; filed small because it partly offsets finding 1 rather than adding a new number.
findings.independence: Finviz preview 2026-10-26 (same document as findings 1-2). FX data for Q3 2026 conflicting across low-quality sources (https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/EUR-USD-2026), so no independent series confirms the size.

findings.finding: Casgevy ramp: revenue $43m in Q1 2026 and $76m in Q2 (+78% q/q, +151% y/y), more than 100 patient initiations for three straight quarters, and FDA extended the label to age 2+; but management warned infusions are variable quarter to quarter in 2026. The non-CF guide of >= $500m (Casgevy + Journavx) needs H2 of roughly $300m against ~$200m in H1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Casgevy $17m vs $42m consensus was cited as the reason the stock fell on that print (-1.0% close, -5.4% peak).
findings.why_not_priced: The initiation backlog (100+ a quarter) feeds infusions with a multi-month lag, which supports sequential growth; the variability warning keeps consensus cautious. Under 3% of revenue, so sized net of the CF franchise that sets the print.
findings.independence: Vertex Q2 release: https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results ; preview noting initiations >100 for three quarters: https://finviz.com/news/408004/vertex-heads-into-q3-with-raised-guidance-as-casgevi-and-gernavix-ramps-face-proof-test

findings.finding: Journavx: Q2 revenue $50m (+71% q/q) on ~535k prescriptions (+45% q/q), covered lives ~260m, and gross-to-net normalisation pushed into H1 2027, which keeps 2026 net price per script higher than a normalising launch; no independent IQVIA weekly series was found for Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Journavx $19.6m vs ~$23m consensus contributed to a sold print (-1.0%).
findings.why_not_priced: Company-reported trajectory only; without script data the street extrapolates, and the delayed GTN step is easy to miss in a per-script model. Small relative to $3.4bn revenue, sized net of CF.
findings.independence: Finviz preview 2026-10-26 for covered lives and GTN timing: https://finviz.com/news/408004/vertex-heads-into-q3-with-raised-guidance-as-casgevi-and-gernavix-ramps-face-proof-test

findings.finding: Pipeline items guided for H2 2026 that may arrive with the release: VX-828 CF proof-of-concept (Phase 1 primary completion 2026-07-10 on ClinicalTrials.gov, no data published), VX-670 DM1 results, and updated zimislecel timelines after the manufacturing-driven dosing pause; each is binary and the zimislecel update leans toward a later filing than the original 2026 target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pipeline news has moved this stock more than quarters: VX-993 pain failure with Q2 2025 -20.6%; inaxaplin data 2026-03-11 +8.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Timing is uncertain (H2 2026, not dated), so the options market prices it only as part of the implied move; no preview found mentions VX-828 or the zimislecel timeline for this call.
findings.independence: Q2 release lists VX-828 PoC H2 2026, VX-670 H2 2026, zimislecel timelines 'later this year': https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results ; Q1 2026 8-K exhibit on zimislecel dosing resumption: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000875320/000087532026000171/ex-991_q12026.htm

baseline_tension: No sealed skew or run-up exists for this name; what is visible (a ~10% pullback from the September high, low short interest, an implied move near 5.5%) neither confirms nor contradicts a small revenue-beat lean offset by a dilutive Crinetics guide.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): revenue-beat/guide finding cut from +1.0 to +0.7 because the Q2 revenue beat with a raised guide bought only +1.7% against a 5.8% implied move.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): EPS bar disputed ($4.80 vs $4.92, plus a stale $4.30), so the EPS/margin finding was capped from -0.8 to -0.5; the revenue bar has two agreeing sources and stands.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): the $4.5bn term loan buys an approved, growing product (Palsonify) plus a Phase 3 asset, not distress; Crinetics guidance finding trimmed from -0.7 to -0.6 and kept as a dilution/guidance item.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): Casgevy and Journavx already sized small relative to a ~95% CF franchise; left standing.
